# Maintaining this profile

The profile is GitHub Markdown with repository-hosted SVG artwork. Twelve project panels, six linked notebook covers in a 3×2 shelf, community work, tools, and a public repository snapshot stay visible on the page. The four research projects each have a full-width row. There are no dropdown interactions, JavaScript, or external stats-card dependencies.

Edit `README.md` for content and links. The generators use Python and Node.js built-in libraries:

```sh
python3 scripts/build_profile.py
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
node tests/physics.test.cjs
```

## Artwork

Midnight gradients, restrained grain, and contour lines connect the panels. GitHub controls the surrounding page background. Separate `<picture>` compositions support phone layouts, and all animation respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.

- `scripts/build_profile.py` composes the header, project panels, constellation, and footer. `scripts/orbital_activity.py` maps public repository recency to elliptical satellite motion and assigns the project-category colors.
- `scripts/mechanical_scenes.py` draws the UAV formations, magnetic switching, and Jackal blueprint. Ten individually colored modules follow smooth Hermite trajectories between delta, spine, and pyramid structures on the public simulator’s lattice. Deterministic approach perturbations, shared drift, rotor-axis thrust marks, and fading sampled tails give the 15-second motion study continuity. Three insets show the assembled configurations. The EPM schematic shows opposite coil-current pulses, the resulting field, core switching, and a flux state that remains latched after current stops.
- The Jackal blueprint uses the official Clearpath J100 mesh edges, the project’s bracket CAD, and public rail, carriage, and joint geometry. Registration guides and pivots explain the exploded system; the two camera mounts face opposite directions. The enlarged camera follows an 18-second 3D yaw/pitch sweep with roll locked. Closed cuboids and capped cylinders retain their surfaces throughout the motion; a small axis key keeps the detail clear. This motion is precomputed into SVG; GitHub’s image renderer supplies no mouse controls. The deck plate renders before the bracket edges to keep the interface visible. Credits and reconstruction details are in [MECHANICAL-SOURCES.md](../data/MECHANICAL-SOURCES.md).
- `scripts/additional_scenes.py` draws the arcade cabinet in perspective, plus the logic circuit, Salem’s Adventure, and software-engineering scenes. `scripts/notebook_cards.py` generates the six linked subject covers.

The illustrations explain the projects. The UAV formations are concept animation, magnetic field lines are schematic, and the point cloud and audio equalizer are decorative. Research descriptions distinguish currently running simulation, ongoing hardware assembly, and a review manuscript in preparation. Upstream and team projects retain their credits. Arcade contribution and responsibility reflect Mohamed’s own account.

The collective-intelligence cover uses a numerically integrated Lorenz trajectory, based on the standard system studied in Gianni A. Di Caro’s Collective Intelligence course materials. Its source-code credit accompanies the original cover rendering; the notebook remains credited as a collaborative fork.

## Public repository snapshot

`python3 scripts/update_activity.py` reads GitHub’s public repository API, stores only repository names, primary languages, and push dates in `data/public-activity.json`, and rebuilds the artwork. `GH_TOKEN` is optional locally; Actions uses its built-in repository token.

The constellation includes public repositories, including forks and the profile repository. Rings mark non-forks and moons mark forks; these indicate repository type, not sole authorship. Their number represents authored commits on the default branch: one for 1–4, two for 5–19, and three for 20 or more; zero and unavailable counts have no marks. Category colors identify research, graphics, coursework, notes, and other work. Newer pushes orbit closer to the center; satellites share a period and are spaced to avoid collisions.

Planet area represents filtered source lines measured with `cloc`, with a minimum visible size; it reflects the whole repository, including collaborators' and upstream code, and is a source-volume proxy rather than a direct measure of complexity. Vendor and generated files are excluded, as are the supplied source-material notebooks in the machine-learning notes repository. Hollow bodies indicate unavailable measurements. The current snapshot contains measurements and authored commit counts for all 25 public repositories. `scripts/refresh_code_metrics.py` and `scripts/refresh_commit_counts.py` refresh these measurements, caching unchanged default-branch heads. Profile updates generated by GitHub Actions retain the previous profile metrics and push date so the automation does not create its own activity loop.

`.github/workflows/refresh-profile.yml` refreshes daily at 03:23 UTC, on manual dispatch, and when generator code changes on `main`. It commits changed artwork and snapshot data. Unchanged metadata retains the snapshot date. API failures preserve existing files and fail visibly. Python tests cover filtering, validation, pagination, unchanged data, and failure behavior. The committed images work without a workflow run; scheduled refreshes start once the workflow reaches GitHub.

Content was reviewed in November 2026 against the current CV, public repositories, and the following primary sources:

- Research: [Modular Multi-UAV Systems](https://github.com/Mohamed-Waiel-Shikfa/Modular_Multi_UAV_Systems), [magsim](https://github.com/Mohamed-Waiel-Shikfa/magsim), [EPM review](https://github.com/Mohamed-Waiel-Shikfa/epm-review), and [Active Vertical Perception](https://github.com/Mohamed-Waiel-Shikfa/Active_Vertical_Perception_System_UGV).
- Graphics: merged CMU Graphics [sound rewrite](https://github.com/cmu-cs-academy/desktop-cmu-graphics/pull/74), [resize fix](https://github.com/cmu-cs-academy/desktop-cmu-graphics/pull/64), and [test maintenance](https://github.com/cmu-cs-academy/desktop-cmu-graphics/pull/100); [R36S](https://github.com/Mohamed-Waiel-Shikfa/r36s_handheld_console), [arcade repository](https://github.com/Mohamed-Waiel-Shikfa/arcade-box-15112), and [logic simulator](https://github.com/Mohamed-Waiel-Shikfa/Edge-project).
- Coursework: [Dim3](https://github.com/Mohamed-Waiel-Shikfa/Dim3), [cofactor experiments](https://github.com/Mohamed-Waiel-Shikfa/Cofactor-Expansion-Research), [Salem’s Adventure](https://github.com/Mohamed-Waiel-Shikfa/Term-project), and the [17-313 team repository](https://github.com/CMU-17313Q/opencode-f26-commitment_issues). The security notebook’s subject follows the official [15-316 course page](https://web2.qatar.cmu.edu/cs/15316/).
- Community: [Open CMUQ](https://github.com/open-cmuq), [Pass the Game](https://github.com/GDC-CMU/PassTheGame), [OpenStack node history](https://review.opendev.org/c/openstack/openstacksdk/+/922610), and [Functional Programming staff](https://web2.qatar.cmu.edu/cs/15150/).
- Milestones: [Class of 2027 scholars](https://www.qatar.cmu.edu/news/cmu-q-names-class-of-2027-qatar-campus-scholars/) and [Meeting of the Minds 2026](https://www.qatar.cmu.edu/news/cmu-qatar-meeting-of-the-minds-2026-undergraduate-research-symposium/).

No private CV or private research artifacts are embedded. The visual direction also draws on the [Awesome GitHub Profile gallery](https://zzetao.github.io/awesome-github-profile/).
